title: ICC issues arrest warrants for Sergei Shoigu and Valery Gerasimov over strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure
body:
On 25 June 2024 the International Criminal Court announced arrest warrants for Sergei Shoigu, then Secretary of Russia's Security Council and formerly defence minister, and Valery Gerasimov, Chief of the General Staff. They are charged with directing attacks at civilian objects, causing excessive incidental harm to civilians or damage to civilian objects, and the crime against humanity of inhumane acts, in connection with Russian strikes on Ukraine's electric infrastructure between October 2022 and March 2023.

The court said there were reasonable grounds to believe that the alleged strikes were directed against civilian objects. It acknowledged that the energy facilities may have been military objectives at the time, but concluded that the expected civilian harm and damage would have been clearly excessive compared with the anticipated military advantage.

Human Rights Watch noted that two other officers, Lieutenant General Sergei Kobylash and Admiral Viktor Sokolov, had received ICC warrants earlier in 2024 for the same set of attacks, and that the court had issued warrants in 2023 for President Vladimir Putin and his children's rights commissioner. Human Rights Watch said the attacks had killed dozens, injured hundreds and left millions without electricity, water and heat. The ICC has no police force and relies on member states to make arrests, and Russia does not recognise its jurisdiction.
